key_insight: Context-Aware Folding (CAF) adds a compressed global risk signal to each local portfolio subproblem, helping hybrid quantum-classical solvers coordinate beyond purely local decomposition.
engineering_relevance: CAF is a lightweight coordination layer that can improve scalability for portfolio optimization while remaining compatible with classical solvers, QAOA, SQA, and NISQ hardware.
method: Inject a global risk state as a state-dependent linear bias into each local subproblem.
Decouple local candidate generation from global commitment using a sequential acceptance rule.
Use a monotonic non-divergence guarantee to preserve stable coordination across folds.
evidence_signal: On a Russell 3000 subset (N=484), CAF with SA improved the scalarized mean-variance objective by 6.59% with 20/20 wins, and on an additional 2018 panel (N=1397) it improved by 0.2579% with 17/20 wins.
watch_item: Performance gains depend on the quality of the compressed global state and the chosen folding/acceptance setup, so hardware and solver compatibility should be validated case by case.
paper_title: A Hybrid Quantum-Classical Coordination Architecture for Portfolio Optimization via Global Context Injection
